title: Grand Theft Auto VI is a love story. No to hiring sex workers, yes to buying your girlfriend flowers

image.caption: Jason and Lucia, the lead characters of Grand Theft Auto VI, can be played as a romantic couple or something more like platonic partners in crime. (Rockstar Games/Take-Two Interactive)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Players jumping into Grand Theft Auto VI today may be surprised that they aren't able to commit some of the more morally objectionable acts that were possible in previous instalments.
Players can build lead couple's romantic relationship instead of hiring prostitutes
This story contains spoilers for the first chapter of Grand Theft Auto VI
The latest game in the series best known as crime and mayhem simulators doesn't let the main characters Jason or Lucia hire sex workers.
Earlier GTA games earned notoriety for letting players pay for a lap dance or sex, and then kill the sex workers and steal the money off their bodies.
Such indignities were possible, though never an objective or featured in the story.

Strippers still feature in GTA VI — both male and female, in a possible series first. An early mission has you talking to club patrons and throwing money at strippers as they dance, sometimes on poles. But you can't hire them for closer encounters.
The reason, Rockstar Games says, is simple: your leading duo are a couple.
Strippers still feature prominently in Grand Theft Auto VI, but the player cannot hire them for sex. (Rockstar Games/Take-Two Interactive)
GTA VI "is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run," the studio said in a statement to the tech site Shack News.

"Many aspects of previous titles are not present… but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia's story."
PHOTOS | Gamers react to GTA VI:

That doesn't mean you're restricted from other kinds of mischief and high-level felonies, of course. Players can choose to play Jason and Lucia as more like platonic partners in crime, and the game still revolves around stealing cars, robbing businesses from corner stores to banks, and escaping the police.

You can still crash into other drivers along the road or even run over unnamed civilians in the city streets — though the consequences could be more severe than in past instalments, as witnesses (or survivors) might call the cops, pull a gun on you themselves, or chase you for kilometres and try to drive you off the road.
A user on Bluesky comments on an early mission in the game in which the player, as Jason, has to buy groceries for Lucia. (UltimaShadow/Bluesky)
As players around the world have gotten their hands on the game, however, some of their first reactions focused on the love story.
After some scene-setting flashbacks, the opening chapter starts with Jason, who's been working odd jobs for a drug dealer named Brian (voiced by Stephen Root).
As he learns that Lucia will soon be released from prison, the player can take time to repair his seaside home: patching up the roof, replacing rotted wooden stairs and painting the bedroom.
All of these actions build up Jason and Lucia's "relationship meter" — the higher the score, the more in sync the two will be throughout their adventures.
Players must manage Jason and Lucia's romantic relationship because how close they are may impact the story. (Rockstar Games/Take-Two Interactive)

Players will find several ways to build their romance; from Jason buying flowers for Lucia before their reunion, to spending more time playing both characters rather than just one. Button prompts make them hold hands while walking together, or simply hug and kiss with multiple animations of the two cuddling or giving a peck on the cheek.
It's a far cry from previous games' protagonists, including GTA V which included Michael, a middle-aged former gangster stuck in a loveless marriage and Trevor, an unhinged psychopath.
It's about family
Jason and Lucia's relationship comes into even greater focus in the early moments of the game.

In a moment of desperation, we see Lucia leave a restaurant to try to rob a nearby payday loans store. It goes poorly and as she's arrested, she shouts that she needs to go back to the restaurant. The camera then shows us a baby carrier with Lucia and Jason's infant son, Tomas.

blocks.text: As the couple reconnect after Lucia's release, they set an objective to make enough money (by doing crime, of course) to put into a family savings account for a future with their son.

That narrative focus flips the usual expectations of a Grand Theft Auto story, and might make a player less likely to engage in the seediest or most violent possible actions compared to in previous games, according to Kotaku writer Kenneth Shepard.

"In some ways, I can see the argument that Jason and Lucia could be willing to go to great lengths to reunite with their son and give him a comfortable life; I’m just not sure I see explosions and constant carnage on the path to that future now," he wrote Thursday, noting that he's only just started playing the game.
Lucia prepares for a robbery early in Grand Theft Auto VI. (Rockstar Games/Take-Two Interactive)
